Sampled-candidate HR@10 cannot establish full-catalog ranking quality: sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). RecSys 2025 research evaluates sampling reliability through resolution, fidelity, robustness and recovery of ground-truth model rankings under controlled exposure conditions ([Pereira et al.](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086)). Implication for RecHarness: preserve the pinned 99-negative evaluator and macro validation HR@10 for selection; compare sampled versus full-catalog validation ranks only as supplementary diagnostics, where permitted. Full-catalog evaluation still does not remove missing-feedback or exposure bias.

Recommended diagnostic design, rather than a validated NextItNet-specific recipe: paired user-level bootstrap intervals, resampling users within each category and recomputing the four-category macro mean; these quantify user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the fixed models and candidates, not training or candidate-sampling variability. Report slice failures divided by slice support, user counts and intervals for history length, training-item frequency and recency; mark unsupported measurements unavailable. This follows the broader emphasis on distributions and uncertainty in [Ekstrand et al. (2024)](https://841.io/doc/disteval.html). Validate probes using diagnostic-only perturbations: shuffle histories, truncate older events, or corrupt the final-position readout, then check sensitivity and specificity against unperturbed controls. Treat order sensitivity as evidence to investigate dilated causal convolutions, long-history degradation as a receptive-field hypothesis, and rare-item failures as a sampling/loss hypothesis—not causal proof. Confirm proposed repairs through controlled ablations within one NextItNet model per category. No directly matching 2024–2026 study establishing this complete diagnostic protocol was identified.
